MOZAMBIQUE 18 MONTHS ON

By: Nicky Troll | Paid

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The insurgency in Mozambique is far from over. The war wages on killing and displacing locals. We ask what South Africa’s links are to ISIS and whether or not there is an ISIS link threat in our bac

Summary:
In the last month there’s been 17 attacks – villages destroyed, civilians killed and some even beheaded. It’s gory and the country carries on burning while the world stays silent.

We explore the developments of the last 18 months in Mozambique and ask just how removed South Africa really is from an insurgent led threat linked to ISIS.

Further information:
18 months after insurgents attacked Cabo del Gado, in Northern Mozambique – attacks continue unabated despite the intervention of SADC and Rwandan troops to shore up the Mozambican military. People are slaughter. Property destroyed. And the threat is not subsiding. It’s moving West and South, gaining momentum and financial support. Security insiders have made linked South African businessmen to funding ISIS operations in Mozambique – these same people have been sanctioned by the Unites States.

We look at the status quo – we speak to security insiders, locals and South Africans that were stuck in the midst of the March 2021 attacks who reflect on it all.

UNPACKING THE MASSCARES THAT WERE EMINENT
By looking retrospectively at the attacks – security analysts have tracked and traced how the attacks were brewing and the Mozambican government failed to take action or at least warn civilians and foreigners in the area.

WHERE DO MOZAMBICAN TURN?
Over 800 000 residents have since fled the area following violent clashes, and 2 800 have died, according to a United Nations report. The conflict has triggered an acute humanitarian crisis and many of its underlying drivers: such as extreme income inequality, endemic corruption and widespread organized crime remain unchanged

We speak to locals – in a lot of the media coverage reports focuses on expats but the vast majority of affected people were locals, who has nowhere to flee – that region was home.

THE PLOT THICKENS - SUSPECTED SUPPORTERS IN SOUTH AFRICA
Two South African men, an Ethiopian national and a Tanzanian have been fingered for helping the ISIS terror group to secure funding. One of the South Africans was previously charged in a case linked to terror-related accusations. The case was eventually dropped.

• Farhad Hoomer (46), who has established an ISIS cell in Durban - Hoomer is alleged to have recruited and trained cell members and was in contact with members of ISIS-Democratic Republic of the Congo (ISIS-DRC) and ISIS supporters throughout South Africa. Hoomer apparently raised funds through kidnap-for-ransom operations and the extortion of major businesses, which provided more than R1 million in revenue for his cell.
• Siraaj Miller (45), leader of a group of ISIS supporters in Cape Town
• Abdella Hussein Abadigga (48), originally from Ethiopia, who recruited young men in South Africa and sent them to a weapons training camp; and
• Peter Charles Mbaga (46), a Tanzanian citizen, who facilitated funds transfers from South Africa - Mbaga is listed for securing funds and weapons for ISIS extremists in the north of Mozambique by using local institutions.

** I suggest we focus on the South African links (Hoomer & Miller – then it’s two RORs)

WHAT IMPACT HAS THE SADC MILITARY MISSION HAD AT WHAT COST?
South African soldiers, together with others in the Southern African Development Community (SADC), are involved in the battle to clear up the bloody Islamic insurgency in Cabo Delgado, Mozambique. In July, the SA government deployed 1 500 SANDF troops to the Cabo Delgado region following calls for assistance from the Mozambique government who have been fighting Jihadists in the gas-rich region.

At least 11 SADC soldiers, including a South African, have been killed in the intervention.
Corporal Tebogo Edwin Radebe, was killed in December 2021 in an ambush on troops by armed insurgents while waiting for air extraction in the Cabo Delgado region of Mozambique. In the last month another SANDF solier was killed and 6 more injured. Experts feel the SANDF is not equipped to fight off insurgence.


INTERVIEWS

- JOE VAN DER WALT – Security Company on the ground in Mozambique – firsthand account and access to all their maps and data tracking the attacks over the last few years.
- INSIDER – SECURITY INSIDER that will explain the connection of ISIS Linked South Africans financing ISIS ops. They have proof but are not at liberty to share this with their identity shown.
- JULIAN RADEMEYER – GITOC – Global Initiative did a report on Insurgency, illicit Markets and corruption in Feb 2022. They cover a whole element on ISIS networks in SA.
- PIERS PIGOU – CRISIS GROUP – International researcher – Peirs is able to comments on the status quo there, the impact the SADC military complement has had on the insurgency.

FOOTAGE
We have some clips from last year’s piece, we have access to 2018 Mosque story CB did. And we have new terror style videos out of Mozambique and also some general visuals shot for us by Joe when he was in Mozambique last week.

STRUCTURE: MOZAMBIQUE ATTACKS 2022

MUSIC MOMENT OVER VISUALS

WES: It's something out of a movie.

VO: Last year Cabo Delgado in Northern Mozambique became the centre of a brutal attack led by the Islamic State terror group.

WES: It still doesn't feel real what happened there.

VO: Wes Nel worked as a construction sub-contractor in Palma, alongside his step-father and brother, Adrian. In a dramatic attempt to escape their hideout at a hotel- Adrian was killed in an ambush.

He was one of dozens who died in March last year, as more than 10 000 locals and foreigners fled the violence.

As the dust settled, the international media packed up and left.

With reports of illicit finance flowing to Islamic State Networks, including from South Africa, it’s clear the insurgency is far from over - the war rages on.

LINK: Villages destroyed. Civilians killed. Some even beheaded. All while the rest of the world seemingly looks away and remains silent.

JOE: The insurgents have become much more brazen. it is problematic// it's not PONTO DUORO sitting next to the ocean. It is a completely different world.

VO: Joe van der Walt provides intelligence driven security solutions in Mozambique. His company’s been tracking the attacks since 2017.

JOE: this is a combination of insurgency led attacks, but also of military action that is taking place.

VO: From 505 attacks in 2020, the number jumped to 548 in 2021 and just half way through 2022 – there’ve already been 307 attacks.

PIGOU: // this insurgency has elevated and has accelerated much faster than all the other comparable insurgencies across across the continent.

VO: Piers Pigou is from the International Crisis Group – conservatively it’s estimated that well over 4000 people have died since the insurgency began.

PIGOU: We think it could be much higher. // not every case is reported// What we have seen with a great deal of brutality is attacks on particularly Mozambican security forces and some pretty horrific video material of people being chopped up, which is part of the kind of designed to to imbue terror and to get people to flee.

VO: Disturbing images and footage have been leaked from Mozambique, and their contents are grotesque. So shocking, infact, that we can’t show most of it.

Strewn throughout rural villages are decapitated and dismembered bodies. Bloodied arms… legs….torsos… heads…. hacked and left for all to see.

LINK: These violent attacks have continued unabated despite intervention from foreign military. The threat is just not subsiding. In fact, they've moved west and south, gaining momentum.

VO: In June, a new wave of violence raged through the Cabo Delgado Province targeting some areas for the first time. Displacing more than 60 0000 ( ) people and claiming at least 50 lives in a single month . The dead include local villagers, security forces and employees from foreign mining companies.

It’s an assault in which civilian discontent is now entwined with the Islamic State’s violent ambitions.

JOE: I think at this point in time, they are linked. They cannot be seen as separately anymore.

VO: In May, the Islamic State declared an independent province in Mozambique, opening a direct reporting line to the central structures outside the country.

ALASTAIR: // it's going through a rapid evolution right now, definitely with this expansion,

VO: Alastair Nelson is from the Global Initiative against Transnational Organized Crime .

ALASTAIR: \ if we look at global politics, the issues to do with global energy //that may be why we're seeing them declaring this as a province. And we see a very faster relationship between attacks happening on the ground and then appearing in IS media.

VO: The images are gruesome. Islamic State soldiers holding a man’s head, posing for pictures. In June alone at least 17 attacks were claimed by the Islamic State.

LINK: Because reporting freely from the ground in Northern Mozambique is near impossible, the atrocities suffered by locals are not being exposed – they’re living in fear – scarred by the attacks and afraid to speak out.

JOE: A lady, her husband, was decapitated. She had to carry the head of her late husband on top of her head. Walking around in the village, telling them that they will be beheaded if they don't leave or, you know, join the fight for ISIS,
MASA: SJOH, Sounds brutal.
JOE: It is brutal.

VO: These incidents have been verified by Van der Walt’s extensive in-country network of sources.

A counterinsurgency operation saw the deployment of 5000 foreign troops from Rwanda and SADC alongside the Mozambican military in July 2021, covering an 80 000 square kilometre region.

PIGOU: // Insurgent capacities have been degraded // major bases have been knocked out, and the insurgents are on the move, hiding in the dense forests //But this hasn't ended the insurgency in any way whatsoever. The instability that the government thought it was getting a handle on is actually now seriously under question.

LINK: The Islamic State has a global network. It's not restricted to a particular region. It transcends borders. And while Islamic radical networks aren't widespread in South Africa, they do exist.

ALASTAIR: //South Africa plays much more of a role in financing that there are definitely IS networks here. // expatriates from all over Africa and other countries come to South Africa to earn money and take it back. There's no reason why criminals and extremists wouldn't be doing the same thing as well.

VO: International bodies have raised concerns around South Africa’s ability to tackle illicit financing flows. Failing to clamp down, could have dire consequences for the country - financially and economically - through what is known as greylisting.

In March the United States Treasury imposed sanctions against what they say are four South African-based ISIS Organizers and Financial Facilitators.

One of these men is Farhad Hoomer.

ALASTAIR: He's a complex character. // he says, // he's not involved in in extremist violence. // but we know that // his name comes up and is tied to a number of incidents that have happened

VO: Hoomer was criminally charged in the 2018 Verulam mosque attack in KZN, later he also faced charges after a warehouse raid where ammunition and weapons were recovered. Now there’s the US Treasury designation.

We called Farhad Hoomer for an on the record response.

HOOMER: I know my name is coming all the time – why? Why is my name popping up

VO: A Security Insider with intimate knowledge of on-going multi-national investigations, confirms that names don’t just pop up

INSIDER: the one that stood out is Mr. FarHAD Hoomer // he's a person of interest. in South Africa, He's deeply involved.
MASA: So do you have concrete evidence that cannot be disputed?
INSIDER: Yup. We managed to obtain proof of illicit transactions. // through front companies

VO: Hoomer denies all the allegations. The South African criminal charges against him have been dropped and he is currently suing the police for damages.

HOOMER: // I’m not a criminal, I am a businessman - I haven’t been found guilty for one crime. // We’re actually trying to sue the FBI because they've got sanctions. Against me

MASA: WHAT ARE THE CHANCES THAT THEY GOT IT WRONG ?
JOE: To actually publish names of South Africans in a report like that will carry weight. There is no way that they will just on a limb, go out and publish names of South Africans.

VO: Apart from the US Treasury List - there are other definite links to Islamic State funding originating from South AFrica.

INSIDER: We identify in excess of ten people Within South Africa of working on this illegal funding.
MASA: What are the chances that you've got it wrong? //
INSIDER: //We've identified a number of suspects through multiple sources. // not known to each other. And then also, we're not talking about one or two transactions. We're talking about multiple transactions over a 3 to 4 year period.
MASA: So you're completely certain we've got the right guys here?
INSIDER: Yeah, I have. M14

PIGOU: // The public deserves more to be taken into the confidence of the intelligence services about what we're really dealing with here. It's not about frightening people and trying to panic, but it is about being realistic about the nature of these relationships. M2M2

VO: While there’s little threat of a similar Islamic State assault on South Africa, our economy could still suffer.

PIGOU: The evolving capacity of these groups should concern us. In the immediate economic concerns related to the LNG sector and southern Africa's energy plans for the future, and that should really worry us//
JOE: I do not believe that the whole problem is fully comprehended and appreciated. it is definitely being downplayed, you know, for whatever reason.

END



 
PROMOS

PROMO 1 – 21 seconds
VO: The Mozambique insurgency linked to the Islamic State is hugely under reported. Every month, villages are destroyed and people brutally killed.

JOE: The insurgents have become much more brazen.

VO: You might think, South Africa is far removed from these extremist networks, but they do exist.

ALASTAIR: South Africa plays much more of a role in financing that there are definitely IS networks here.

PROMO 2 - 21 seconds
VO: A new wave of violence, driven by Islamic State linked insurgents, rages through Mozambique.

PIGOU: this insurgency has elevated and has accelerated much faster than all the other comparable insurgencies across across the continent.

VO: But how far removed is South Africa from these radical networks?


PROMO 3 – 11 seconds
VO: The Mozambique insurgency linked to the Islamic State - is FAR from over – every month, villages are destroyed and civilians killed. It’s all on our doorstep but could there be sinister links in our own backyard?




STUDIO INTRO
On the anniversary of the foreign military deployment….

ALASTAIR: He's a complex character. // he says, // he's not involved in in extremist violence. // but we know that // his name comes up and is tied to a number of incidents that have happened VO: Hoomer was criminally charged in the 2018 Verulam mosque attack in KZN, later he also faced charges after a warehouse raid where ammunition and weapons were recovered. Now there’s the US Treasury designation. We called Farhad Hoomer for an on the record response. HOOMER: I know my name is coming all the time – why? Why is my name popping up VO: A Security Insider with intimate knowledge of on-going multi-national investigations, confirms that names don’t just pop up INSIDER: the one that stood out is Mr. FarHAD Hoomer // he's a person of interest. in South Africa, He's deeply involved. MASA: So do you have concrete evidence that cannot be disputed? INSIDER: Yup. We managed to obtain proof of illicit transactions. // through front companies VO: Hoomer denies all the allegations. The South African criminal charges against him have been dropped and he is currently suing the police for damages. HOOMER: // I’m not a criminal, I am a businessman - I haven’t been found guilty for one crime. // We’re actually trying to sue the FBI because they've got sanctions. Against me MASA: WHAT ARE THE CHANCES THAT THEY GOT IT WRONG ? JOE: To actually publish names of South Africans in a report like that will carry weight. There is no way that they will just on a limb, go out and publish names of South Africans. VO: Apart from the US Treasury List - there are other definite links to Islamic State funding originating from South AFrica. INSIDER: We identify in excess of ten people Within South Africa of working on this illegal funding. And then also, we're not talking about one or two transactions. We're talking about multiple transactions over a 3 to 4 year period. MASA: So you're completely certain we've got the right guys here? INSIDER: Yeah, I have. M14 PIGOU: // The public deserves more to be taken into the confidence of the intelligence services about what we're really dealing with here. It's not about frightening people and trying to panic, but it is about being realistic about the nature of these relationships. In the immediate economic concerns related to the LNG sector and southern Africa's energy plans for the future, and that should really worry us// JOE: I do not believe that the whole problem is fully comprehended and appreciated. it is definitely being downplayed, you know, for whatever reason. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): The insurgency in Mozambique is far from over. The war wages on killing and displacing locals. We ask what South Africa’s links are to ISIS and whether or not there is an ISIS link threat in our bac
metadata.Summary: In the last month there’s been 17 attacks – villages destroyed, civilians killed and some even beheaded. It’s gory and the country carries on burning while the world stays silent. We explore the developments of the last 18 months in Mozambique and ask just how removed South Africa really is from an insurgent led threat linked to ISIS.
metadata.Further information: 18 months after insurgents attacked Cabo del Gado, in Northern Mozambique – attacks continue unabated despite the intervention of SADC and Rwandan troops to shore up the Mozambican military. People are slaughter. Property destroyed. And the threat is not subsiding. It’s moving West and South, gaining momentum and financial support. Security insiders have made linked South African businessmen to funding ISIS operations in Mozambique – these same people have been sanctioned by the Unites States. We look at the status quo – we speak to security insiders, locals and South Africans that were stuck in the midst of the March 2021 attacks who reflect on it all. UNPACKING THE MASSCARES THAT WERE EMINENT By looking retrospectively at the attacks – security analysts have tracked and traced how the attacks were brewing and the Mozambican government failed to take action or at least warn civilians and foreigners in the area. WHERE DO MOZAMBICAN TURN? Over 800 000 residents have since fled the area following violent clashes, and 2 800 have died, according to a United Nations report. The conflict has triggered an acute humanitarian crisis and many of its underlying drivers: such as extreme income inequality, endemic corruption and widespread organized crime remain unchanged We speak to locals – in a lot of the media coverage reports focuses on expats but the vast majority of affected people were locals, who has nowhere to flee – that region was home. THE PLOT THICKENS - SUSPECTED SUPPORTERS IN SOUTH AFRICA Two South African men, an Ethiopian national and a Tanzanian have been fingered for helping the ISIS terror group to secure funding. One of the South Africans was previously charged in a case linked to terror-related accusations. The case was eventually dropped. • Farhad Hoomer (46), who has established an ISIS cell in Durban - Hoomer is alleged to have recruited and trained cell members and was in contact with members of ISIS-Democratic Republic of the Congo (ISIS-DRC) and ISIS supporters throughout South Africa. Hoomer apparently raised funds through kidnap-for-ransom operations and the extortion of major businesses, which provided more than R1 million in revenue for his cell. • Siraaj Miller (45), leader of a group of ISIS supporters in Cape Town • Abdella Hussein Abadigga (48), originally from Ethiopia, who recruited young men in South Africa and sent them to a weapons training camp; and • Peter Charles Mbaga (46), a Tanzanian citizen, who facilitated funds transfers from South Africa - Mbaga is listed for securing funds and weapons for ISIS extremists in the north of Mozambique by using local institutions. ** I suggest we focus on the South African links (Hoomer & Miller – then it’s two RORs) WHAT IMPACT HAS THE SADC MILITARY MISSION HAD AT WHAT COST? South African soldiers, together with others in the Southern African Development Community (SADC), are involved in the battle to clear up the bloody Islamic insurgency in Cabo Delgado, Mozambique. In July, the SA government deployed 1 500 SANDF troops to the Cabo Delgado region following calls for assistance from the Mozambique government who have been fighting Jihadists in the gas-rich region. At least 11 SADC soldiers, including a South African, have been killed in the intervention. Corporal Tebogo Edwin Radebe, was killed in December 2021 in an ambush on troops by armed insurgents while waiting for air extraction in the Cabo Delgado region of Mozambique. In the last month another SANDF solier was killed and 6 more injured. Experts feel the SANDF is not equipped to fight off insurgence. INTERVIEWS - JOE VAN DER WALT – Security Company on the ground in Mozambique – firsthand account and access to all their maps and data tracking the attacks over the last few years. - INSIDER – SECURITY INSIDER that will explain the connection of ISIS Linked South Africans financing ISIS ops. They have proof but are not at liberty to share this with their identity shown. - JULIAN RADEMEYER – GITOC – Global Initiative did a report on Insurgency, illicit Markets and corruption in Feb 2022. They cover a whole element on ISIS networks in SA. - PIERS PIGOU – CRISIS GROUP – International researcher – Peirs is able to comments on the status quo there, the impact the SADC military complement has had on the insurgency. FOOTAGE We have some clips from last year’s piece, we have access to 2018 Mosque story CB did. And we have new terror style videos out of Mozambique and also some general visuals shot for us by Joe when he was in Mozambique last week.
